newsitem.title: INDIA: India L&T completes platform for oil firm.
newsitem.headline: India L&T completes platform for oil firm.

text.p: Indian engineering and construction firm Larsen & Toubro said it completed a $27 million process platform for Enron Oil and Gas India Ltd. "The platform, weighing about 2,000 tonnes, is the single largest offshore marine structure to be fabricated and assembled in India," the company said in a statement.

Enron Oil and Gas India is operated by Enron Oil and Gas Company of the U.S. which has a 30 percent interest. The state-run Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Ltd owns 40 percent and petrochemicals firm Reliance Industries Ltd 30 percent.
Larsen said the process platform, equivalent in height to a six-storey building, was delivered under a contract valued at $27.0 million secured under a global bidding.
The platform has been handed over to Enron's production group and is now under final start-up operations, it said.
Enron's Tapti offshore project is 60 km west of Surat on the western coast. The platform is designed to handle five million cubic metres of gas and 3,000 barrels of oil per day.
Larsen had earlier executed well-head platforms for extracting crude oil. The Enron platform helps to process the crude oil received from well-head platforms, it said.
